name: sc-1775
title: South Carolina, 1775-1781: reconstructed base map (WarMapper)
note: A WarMapper reconstruction, not a period map: the main lines of Mouzon's map of 1775, fitted to the ground. See pipeline/recon/sc_1775.py. [longitude, latitude], WGS 84.

properties.name: Cherokee boundary line (1766)
properties.basis: Mouzon's line (Mouzon 1775 (S135), Library of Congress g3900.ar139404), picked by hand; the North Carolina lines were fitted to today's state line, which follows them (Natural Earth, S136). Mouzon draws it from the Savannah at a corner tree, past DeWitt's Corner, to a corner tree on the Reedy River and north to the 1772 line. The Cherokee ceded the land east of it in 1766-67 and nearly all the rest in South Carolina at DeWitt's Corner, 20 May 1777, so it is drawn until then.

properties.name: Path from the Cherokees to the Catawba Nation
properties.desc: Path from the Cherokees to the Catawba Nation
properties.basis: Traced along Mouzon's double line (Mouzon 1775 (S135), Library of Congress g3900.ar139404): snapped by program to the gap between the two engraved lines, from end to end, within about 2 km of the hand-picked line, and checked by eye (pipeline/recon/sc_1775_roads_2026_11_26.py, 26 Nov 2026). Its ends are joined to the road or town it meets where Mouzon draws them meeting (another road within 3 km, a town within 6.5 km). Laid on the ground by the fit of the map: within about 1 km at the towns the fit holds (Camden, Orangeburg, Charles Town, Georgetown, Dorchester, Beaufort, Ninety Six, Long Bluff), about 3-5 km between them.
